question: If the length, breadth, and height of a rectangular parallelepiped are 5 cm, 4 cm, and 3 cm, its volume is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a rectangular parallelepiped = Product of its three dimensions

Volume = Length × Breadth × Height

Volume = 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm

Volume = 60 cm³

**∴ Answer = 60 cm³**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length (l) = 5 cm

Breadth (b) = 4 cm

Height (h) = 3 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of a cuboid (Rectangular Parallelepiped) = l × b × h

 
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 Length (l) = 5 cm
 Breadth (b) = 4 cm
 Height (h) = 3 cm
 Volume = l × b × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = Length × Breadth × Height

⇒ Volume = 5 × 4 × 3

⇒ Volume = 20 × 3

⇒ Volume = 60 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm³, which is option (1).**</p
